what-helm-is-and-why-use-it.r: A team maintained nearly identical YAML for three environments, and a change was forgotten in one of them. A chart with a few values per environment kept the shape the same everywhere.
what-helm-is-and-why-use-it.x: Helm packages and versions applications, but it adds templating you must debug. Use it where reuse and release management pay off, and be wary of charts you do not understand.

installing-charts-and-values.r: An engineer installed a public chart with default values and exposed an admin interface. Reading the default values and overriding them first would have kept it private.
installing-charts-and-values.x: Read a chart before you run it: defaults, images, permissions and hooks. Pin chart and image versions, keep your overrides in a file under version control and review the rendered output.

anatomy-of-a-chart.r: A new chart copied from a template still carried placeholder values and an unused service account. A review of each file in the chart removed the leftovers before release.
anatomy-of-a-chart.x: Keep charts small and honest: only template what varies, put defaults in values, document them and include tests. Version the chart separately from the application.

templates-and-the-go-template-language.r: A template with nested conditions rendered invalid YAML for one rare combination of values. Rendering with several value sets in CI caught it before release.
templates-and-the-go-template-language.x: Template logic should be simple. Use helpers for repeated code, handle indentation carefully and test rendering with edge-case values, including empty ones.

upgrade-rollback-and-release-history.r: An upgrade failed halfway and left a release in a pending state. Using atomic upgrades with a timeout, and checking the history, allowed an automatic rollback to the last good revision.
upgrade-rollback-and-release-history.x: Rollback restores manifests, not data. Plan database changes separately, keep enough history, use wait and atomic options in pipelines and know how to recover a stuck release.

values-per-environment-and-secrets.r: A password was placed in a values file and committed. Moving secrets to an external secret manager, with the chart referencing them, kept values files safe to review.
values-per-environment-and-secrets.x: Keep environment differences small and visible. Never store secrets in values in plain text, and avoid a layering of values files so deep that nobody knows what ends up applied.

dependencies-subcharts-and-registries.r: A subchart update changed a default and altered a production setting unexpectedly. Pinning dependency versions with a lock file and reviewing diffs on update made upgrades deliberate.
dependencies-subcharts-and-registries.x: Dependencies are supply chain. Pin and lock them, mirror what you rely on, sign charts and understand which values flow into subcharts.

debugging-helm-releases.r: An install failed with a vague message. Rendering the templates locally showed an indentation error, and the dry-run caught the next one before it reached the cluster.
debugging-helm-releases.x: Render, lint and diff before applying. Look at hooks and tests when a release hangs, compare live objects with rendered ones and keep a record of manual changes that Helm would overwrite.

testing-and-linting-helm-charts.r: A chart change removed a required label and the rendered manifest was rejected only when it reached production. Adding rendering and schema checks to CI caught the same mistake in minutes.
testing-and-linting-helm-charts.x: A broken chart breaks many deployments at once. Automated checks at the chart level are cheap protection for everyone who uses it.

library-charts-and-chart-reuse.r: A security fix to the pod template required editing forty charts. After moving to a library chart, the fix was one change plus a version bump in each service.
library-charts-and-chart-reuse.x: Reuse saves effort and creates coupling. Keep shared templates small, versioned and well tested, because every consumer inherits their mistakes.

publishing-and-signing-helm-charts.r: Someone overwrote a chart version in the registry with a different build. Immutable tags and signatures made that detectable and then impossible. Afterwards the team added a check to catch the same problem earlier. The fix was small once the cause was clear, and the team wrote it down.
publishing-and-signing-helm-charts.x: Treat chart repositories like package repositories: authenticated writes, immutable versions and verified reads.

helm-security-and-supply-chain.r: A popular chart from the internet defaulted to a privileged container and a cluster role with wide rights. A rendered-manifest scan flagged it, and the team overrode the settings before install.
helm-security-and-supply-chain.x: Installing a chart is running someone else's configuration with your credentials. Verify it like you would any dependency.
